rows.analysis_unit: lesion (abstract reports lesions treated vs baseline and untreated lesions; lesion counts not in abstract)
rows.intervention: excimer laser for 12 weeks using the vitiligo protocol
rows.endpoint_definition: repigmentation graded by blinded observer scale through photographic comparisons
rows.assessment_method: blinded observer scale from photographs at end of study; participant self-grading at intervals; descriptive trend analysis and ANOVA
rows.time_from_start: end of study (treatment lasted 12 weeks; study length not in abstract)
rows.time_from_last_treatment: not in abstract (graded 'at the end of the study'; interval after final treatment not stated)
rows.arm_result: treated lesions had significantly higher repigmentation by the end of the study than baseline and untreated lesions; no numbers in abstract
rows.patient_noticeability: participants graded progress at intervals; results not in abstract
rows.uncertainty: Abstract only; full text paywalled (Europe PMC: subscription required; LWW 403). No effect size, lesion count or follow-up after final treatment in abstract. Abstract does not say whether 'end of the study' is the final treatment visit or later, so months after final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE. Abstract does not name a trial registration; registry record NCT01956435 is a separate unit and was not used.
rows.citation: Gordon JR, Reed KE, Sebastian KR, Ahmed AM. Dermatol Surg 2017;43(4):553-557

quotes.quote: 6 patients were treated with excimer laser for 12 weeks using the vitiligo protocol
Lesions that received the excimer treatment had significantly higher repigmentation by the end of the study compared with baseline and untreated lesions.
Effectiveness was graded by the blinded observer scale through photographic comparisons at the end of the study.

verifier.notes: row 0, uncertainty: the source states this is a 'pilot study' in which '6 patients were treated', and the significance claim is made for 'Lesions that received the excimer treatment' with 'an ANOVA model'; uncertainty does not record the very small sample (6 patients), nor that lesions were analysed while several lesions come from each of only 6 patients (clustering within patients not addressed in the text), nor that one comparison is against 'baseline' rather than only untreated lesions, nor that the Conclusion's 'acceptable cosmetic outcomes' is not backed by any reported result. All other cells match the source text; outcome_tier partial_repigmentation and months_after_final_tx NOT_DERIVABLE are supported.
